author: DecoySnake
quote:
0/10 — A grotesque and unnecessary remake of a masterpiece

The original Ocarina of Time was a groundbreaking adventure. This remake takes that masterpiece, strips away some of what made it special and replaces it with baffling design choices, unnecessary additions and some genuinely uncomfortable imagery.

My biggest criticism isn't even the simplified dungeons, excessive handholding, redesigned inventory or missing Master Quest. It's how downright weird this remake feels.

The new cutscenes and character designs are frequently grotesque. We've got Moblins redesigned with exposed backsides and leather straps, complete with Navi drawing attention to their lack of rear armour. Jabu-Jabu's Belly features increasingly organic, orifice-like doors alongside the wonderfully unfortunate “Shoot Seed” prompt. Then there's the questionable low-angle cinematography involving Young Link.

Individually, people can dismiss these as harmless. Taken together, I find the choices bizarre, unnecessary and tonally inappropriate. Why introduce imagery and dialogue that can reasonably be interpreted as suggestive into a remake aimed at a family audience?

What's especially strange is that the 2011 3DS version carried an ESRB “Suggestive Themes” descriptor, yet this remake doesn't. I think that discrepancy deserves an explanation.

Meanwhile, elements that actually served the original adventure have been simplified or removed. Puzzles require less thought, the darker atmosphere has been softened, Master Quest is absent, and mechanics that were groundbreaking in 1998 are replaced or supplemented with features that don't meaningfully improve the experience.

I'm not claiming the remake is broken or unplayable. Of course it can still be enjoyable — it's built on one of the greatest games ever made.

But inheriting a masterpiece doesn't make your changes masterpieces.

I don't consider this a definitive edition. I consider it an inferior, unnecessarily sanitised and occasionally grotesque version **** that was already better designed.

The original deserved better.
